body.input: Which government or defence contracts and public funding agreements has ICEYE signed since 2025? List the counterparty, date and value of each.

response.content:
## ICEYE – Government, Defence & Public Funding Agreements Since 2025

Below is a summary of the key contracts, procurement agreements, and public funding deals ICEYE has signed since the start of 2025, based on available reporting.

| # | Counterparty | Date | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Polish Armed Forces** (Ministry of National Defence) | May 2025 | Procurement of 3 SAR satellites under the MicroSAR programme | ~€200 million |
| 2 | **IHI Corporation (Japan)** | 22 May 2025 | MoU to develop a SAR constellation of up to 24 satellites (signed at DSEI Japan) | Not disclosed |
| 3 | **Finnish Defence Forces** | 8 September 2025 | Procurement of sovereign SAR satellite system (satellites, ground systems, options for expansion) | ~€158 million |
| 4 | **IHI Corporation (Japan)** | 16 October 2025 | Procurement contract for an initial 4 satellites (option for 20 more), building on the May MoU; completion targeted by FY2029 | Not disclosed |
| 5 | **Portugal, the Netherlands & NATO** | Late 2025 (within a two-week period) | Three separate defence agreements for SAR data / ISR capabilities | Not disclosed |
| 6 | **Finnish Ministry of Defence / Netherlands / Poland** | December 2025 | Letter of intent on trilateral SAR satellite cooperation | Not disclosed |
| 7 | **German Armed Forces (BAAINBw)** via **Rheinmetall ICEYE Space Solutions** JV | 18 December 2025 | "SPOCK 1" – space-based SAR reconnaissance constellation; contract runs end-2025 to end-2030 with extension options | ~€1.7 billion |
| 8 | **Swedish Defence Materiel Administration (FMV)** | 12 January 2026 | Multi-year sovereign SAR satellite system for the Swedish Armed Forces (satellites, data, software, ground systems) | Multi-million euro (exact figure not disclosed) |
| 9 | **Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego (BGK), Poland** (via Vinci fund) | 2026 | Investment / loan to support ICEYE's R&D and production facilities in Poland | PLN 40 million (~$11 million) |
| 10 | **Hellenic Innovation & Infrastructure Fund (HIIF), Greece** | 2025–2026 | Strategic investment in ICEYE (first HIIF investment); linked to planned satellite manufacturing plant in Attica | €35 million |
| 11 | **EU SAFE mechanism (Greece component)** | Pending (earmarked) | Joint procurement of SAR satellites with Poland under the EU SAFE defence-funding programme | €80 million earmarked |
| 12 | **Business Finland** | 2026 | Continuation R&D grant (final tranche of a previously announced investment decision) | €28.3 million |
| 13 | **ESA / CBK PAN (Civil Security Hub Poland)** | 12 November 2026 | Subscription contract for flood, wildfire and river-ice monitoring under ESA's European Resilience from Space initiative | Not disclosed |
| 14 | **Ukraine – Letter of Intent** | 2026 | LoI with ICEYE and Nokia for sovereign satellite communications (signed by Ukraine's Ministry of Defence) | Not disclosed |

### Notes
- Several of these agreements (e.g. the IHI MoU, the trilateral LoI, the Ukraine LoI) are framework or pre-contractual instruments rather than binding procurement contracts.
- The SPOCK 1 contract (€1.7 billion) is by far the largest single award; it was placed with the Rheinmetall ICEYE Space Solutions joint venture rather than with ICEYE directly.
- ICEYE also participated in major NATO exercises (ORION 2026, Cold Response 2026) and is expanding U.S. operations through its subsidiary ICEYE US, including a partnership with PAR Government on a $900 million U.S. Space Force PLEO contract vehicle, though the timing and specific ICEYE share of that vehicle are not fully detailed in public sources.

explainability.content: ICEYE signed a procurement contract with the Polish Armed Forces in May 2025 for three SAR satellites valued at approximately €200 million.
ICEYE signed a procurement contract with the Finnish Defence Forces on 8 September 2025 for a sovereign SAR satellite system worth about €158 million, including options for extension.
ICEYE and Japan’s IHI Corporation signed a memorandum of understanding on 22 May 2025 to develop a SAR constellation of up to 24 satellites.
Following the May MOU, ICEYE and IHI signed a procurement contract on 16 October 2025 for an initial four satellites (with an option for 20 more) to be built in Japan.

ICEYE, through the joint venture Rheinmetall ICEYE Space Solutions, received the German Armed Forces “SPOCK 1” contract on 18 December 2025, valued at roughly €1.7 billion and running to end‑20210 with extensions.
ICEYE signed a multi‑year sovereign SAR system contract with the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration on 12 January 2026, described as a multi‑million‑euro agreement.
Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego (BGK) provided a PLN 40 million (~US$11 million) loan to ICEYE in 2026 to support R&D and production facilities in Poland.
The Hellenic Innovation & Infrastructure Fund invested €35 million in ICEYE as its first HIIF investment, linked to a planned satellite plant in Greece.
An €80 million earmark under the EU SAFE mechanism was allocated for the joint SAR satellite procurement involving Greece and Poland.
Business Finland approved a continuation R&D grant of €28.3 million to ICEYE in 2026, the final tranche of a previously announced investment decision.
ICEYE signed a subscription contract with ESA’s Civil Security Hub Poland on 12 November 2026 to provide flood, wildfire and river‑ice monitoring services.

context.content:
What has changed the game is price. ICEYE shrank the radar satellite to roughly a tenth of the size of a traditional reconnaissance satellite and cut the cost to a fraction of what it used to be. This has meant that small and medium-sized countries, not just major powers, can now afford the capability. ICEYE has numerous customers, among them seven NATO member states that have procured sovereign satellite systems, and the company has supported Ukraine since 2022. In January 2026, Sweden became a customer through an agreement with the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration (FMV), making Sweden the first sovereign-system customer in the Nordics besides Finland. [...] The foundation is already in place. In December 2025, the Finnish Ministry of Defence signed a letter of intent with the Netherlands and Poland on cooperation around SAR satellites from ICEYE, and more countries are expected to join. ICEYE already works closely with allies such as Poland, the Netherlands and Germany, and Aaltonen sees the Baltic states as a good fit as well. He believes that Sweden now being a customer means Norway, Denmark and other NATO allies gain a well-proven concept to step into.

"Every time, it gets easier. We build up standards, train the teams, and the alliance becomes more proficient," he says. [...] "The AI can flag a suspected target within a few tens of seconds, and then an analyst reviews it. The human is always kept in the decision loop," he says.

The concept has been tested in exercises. During the major French exercise ORION 2026, ICEYE embedded a mobile ISR (intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance) cell within a French army brigade and fed targeting data into the brigade's sensor-to-shooter chain. The company also took part in Cold Response 2026 in northern Norway, Finland and Sweden, one of the largest NATO exercises in a long time, involving around 30,000 soldiers from 14 nations.

For Aaltonen, this is in line with a Nordic way of fighting.

The sovereign-intelligence demand signal is the structural part. Defense News framed ICEYE’s positioning in November as Europe’s defence space-intelligence linchpin, on the back of contracts signed with the armed forces of Poland, Portugal, the Netherlands and Finland through 2025.

The US’s pause on intelligence-sharing with Ukraine in March 2025 was, on the same coverage, the catalyst that moved European procurement budgets decisively toward sovereign satellite-intelligence capabilities. [...] ‘It also enhances our financial flexibility as demand for sovereign intelligence capabilities continues to grow exponentially.’

On the strategic-capital line, the RCF sits on top of a €150m Series E equity round closed in December 2024, led by US venture firm General Catalyst, and a separate €158m Finnish Defence Forces SAR-satellite supply contract signed in September 2025, covering three satellites with options for additional units. [...] The combination, equity, government-supply contract, and now a senior-bank-syndicate credit line, is the financing stack that lets ICEYE underwrite the multi-year procurement contracts the company is increasingly being asked to write for European and Asia-Pacific defence customers.

Warsaw, Poland – November 12, 2026 –  ICEYE,  the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space, and the Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences (CBK PAN) announced a contract under which ICEYE will supply flood, wildfire, and river ice monitoring to Civil Security Hub Poland (CS Hub PL), Poland’s node in the European Space Agency’s (ESA) Space Resilience Nodes initiative. The agreement gives CS Hub PL standing access to ICEYE disaster monitoring under a subscription model, rather than requiring services to be activated separately for each event. The contract is part of ESA’s European Resilience from Space for Earth Observation (ERS-EO) initiative, which aims to give Europe reliable, secure, timely, “always on” access to independent space-based information during [...] ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.   
  
ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.   
  
ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defense and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future. [...] The contract builds on earlier collaboration between ICEYE, CBK PAN, and ESA, including operational support during Storm Boris in September 2024, an activation already communicated under the Civil Security Hub name. ICEYE delivered flood data every 6 hours to CBK PAN’s Crisis Information Centre, which passed the data to the State Fire Service, regional and local crisis management teams, and hydrological services. Flood Rapid Impact was the main source of flood information during the first four days of the event, according to the Crisis Information Centre. ICEYE developed and matured these flood and wildfire services with ESA and CBK PAN through the COSMOS project under ESA’s Civil Security from Space initiative.
